title: Why Something Rather Than Nothing

canonical_node.axiom: Something exists rather than nothing, and this is undeniable.
definitions: Existence: that which is not nothing; the state of being real.
Nothing: the absence of any existence, including the absence of any properties or distinctions.
Distinguishability: the property of being different from something else; a difference that makes a difference.
Information: the capacity to distinguish states; equivalently, distinguishability.
derivation: If something exists, it must be distinguishable from nothing; otherwise it would be nothing.
P0.2: x,y : x  y (Existence requires distinguishability).
P0.3: H(X) = - p(x) log p(x) (Information primacy).
canonical_node.action: Treat P0.1 as the foundational axiom. Reject any claim that denies existence, as such denial is self-refuting. Use P0.1 as the basis for all subsequent axioms and arguments.
boundary: Does not prove the nature of existence beyond its bare fact.
Does not establish the existence of any particular entity.
Does not derive existence from anything else; it is primitive.
Does not claim that existence is good or purposeful; that is a separate claim.
test: Attempt to deny P0.1 without presupposing existence; if the denial requires a speaker, thinker, or writer, the denial fails.
Check that any proposed 'nothing' is not actually something (e.g., quantum vacuum, imagination).
Verify that any physical theory presupposes existence in its formulation.

dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides an undeniable foundation for all subsequent axioms; establishes that existence is primitive and self-evident.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: No prior floor exists; this is the base.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: If P0.1 is removed, the entire chain collapses; no other axiom can stand without it.

classification.recommended_atom_action: Accept as primitive axiom; do not treat as proven theorem.

overstatement_risks: Claiming that existence is 'undeniable' may be too strong; it is self-evident but not formally proven.
Equating distinguishability with information is a definitional choice, not a proven identity.
Theological interpretations (e.g., 'I AM') are not derivable from the axiom.
kill_conditions: If a coherent model of 'nothing' is shown to be stable and non-self-refuting.
If 'nothing' can be meaningfully predicated without presupposing existence.
risk.lean_target: Formalize P0.1 as a primitive in a logical system; avoid overclaiming its implications.

plain_summary: This document establishes the foundational axiom that something exists, arguing that any denial is self-refuting. It defines existence, nothing, distinguishability, and information, and derives that existence implies distinguishability and information. The document is coherent as a primitive axiom but does not provide a formal proof; it is best treated as a foundational assumption.
